description:
Vincent De Smet built a CDK Terrain workshop that runs entirely on AWS's new, agent-built emulator, and had Fable patch the gaps it found along the way.

Kai Hendry and Vincent tour the workshop box, look at an emulator repository that gets a commit every two minutes, and ask what reviewing code means in the agentic era. They compare Google's elephant and goldfish model, Lauren Tan's verification skill and Matt Pocock's grill-me, then turn to stale company skills, page-long prompts, PII in logs and background agents.

AI Infrastructure — Episode 48
Recorded 17 November 2026.

CHAPTERS
00:00 A view of Saigon, zoning and Belgium
03:49 Config Management Camp and the CDK Terrain community
05:45 A CDK Terrain workshop in Singapore
08:28 Car-free Ghent and hearing horses
12:28 Patching and building the AWS emulator with Fable
18:07 Five gigabytes per workshop attendee
21:57 Caddy, Traefik and Kong
23:28 Inside the workshop box
32:32 Commits every two minutes in the AWS emulator repo
38:59 Reviewing code in the agentic era
40:44 How the clouds are adapting to AI
42:13 Google's elephant and goldfish model
46:53 Lauren Tan's verification skill and Playwright
51:18 Formal verification, comments and TODOs
55:35 Stale skills, gardening and glossaries
59:55 Rethinking Claude Code best practices
1:03:21 Does a page-long prompt beat a simple one?
1:10:10 PII, scoped tokens and break-glass access
1:13:54 Background agents
